articles.title: Tell us: How do you feel about Sweden's government nail-biter?
articles.summary: More than 50 days after the election, Sweden's government negotiations are suddenly moving fast, with the Centre Party currently playing the role of king-maker. What do you think of it all?

articles.title: How Sweden's parties have reacted to the latest political drama
articles.summary: The Sweden Democrats' bombshell decision to drop its demand for cabinet posts and the Centre Party's threat to switch sides sparked a flurry of activity from Sweden's political parties over the weekend. But what are the main players saying?

articles.title: How does the Sweden Democrats' decision to back Kristersson as PM change things?
articles.summary: Far right Sweden Democrat leader Jimmie Åkesson has announced that his party will unconditionally 'tolerate' Ulf Kristersson as prime minister and then go into opposition. What does this mean for the process of forming Sweden's next government?

articles.title: 'You're on your own': Sweden Democrats drop demands to allow Kristersson to be PM
articles.summary: Sweden Democrat leader Jimmie Åkesson has dropped his demand for cabinet posts, announcing his party is willing to tolerate Ulf Kristersson so he can become prime minister.

articles.title: Sweden Democrat leader to give update on ministerial posts
articles.summary: Sweden Democrat leader Jimmie Åkesson is set to hold a press conference in his hometown of Sölvesborg around lunchtime today to address the ongoing government formation talks.

articles.title: Member Q&A: When will Sweden get a new government?
articles.summary: Sweden doesn't have a new government yet, more than 50 days after the election. When will it get one? The Local's editor answered readers' questions.

articles.title: Sweden's outgoing PM Ulf Kristersson to try to form a new government
articles.summary: Sweden's outgoing conservative prime minister Ulf Kristersson has been tasked with trying to form a new government amid a political deadlock more than seven weeks after the country's general election.

articles.title: Swedish parliament rejects Centre Party leader as next prime minister
articles.summary: The Swedish parliament has, as expected, voted against Centre Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist as prime minister. Moderate Party leader Ulf Kristersson will now get the next shot at forming a government.

articles.title: What happens next in the process to form a Swedish government?
articles.summary: It's over 50 days since Sweden's election and formally at least, the political parties have not moved even the tiniest step closer to forming a government. Here's what happens next.

articles.title: 'It will not happen': Top Centre Party MP rules out Sweden Democrat deal
articles.summary: Martin Ådahl, economics spokesperson for the Centre Party, has ruled out any deal which will see his party support a right-wing government dependent on the far-right Sweden Democrats, telling The Local simply that "it will not happen'.

articles.title: 'A lot of arguing to be done': What's at stake in the upcoming EU-UK summit?
articles.summary: Leaders of the EU and the UK will meet for a crucial summit in November with a move towards closer cooperation on the table. But how much will be achieved given the differences and disagreements that exist?

articles.title: OPINION: One Sweden, one 'folk'?
articles.summary: Some Sweden Democrats think the only true Swedes are those who can trace back their ancestry to the dawn of time. It's an extreme idea that collapses under its own contradictions, argues The Local's James Savage.

articles.title: Sweden Democrat leader backs 'open Swedishness' amid high-profile party clash
articles.summary: Sweden Democrat leader Jimmie Åkesson has waded into an ongoing internal party row over what defines Swedish identity.

articles.title: Swedish parliamentary speaker picks Centre Party leader as next PM candidate
articles.summary: Centre Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist is set to face a parliamentary confirmation vote to become Sweden's next prime minister, the speaker of parliament has announced.

articles.title: New poll shows Sweden's Moderate Party just behind Social Democrats
articles.summary: Sweden's Social Democrats have been the largest party in the country for a hundred years. But according to a new opinion poll, the Moderates are closing in.

articles.title: Swedish business sector urges next government to overhaul global talent strategy
articles.summary: A leading Swedish business organisation is urging the next government – whenever it is formed – to step up the work of attracting and retaining crucial international talent.

articles.title: Sweden's right wing takes clear lead over left wing in new poll
articles.summary: Following strong gains for the Moderate Party and the Sweden Democrats, a new poll has the right-wing side nearly four percentage points higher than their left-wing rivals.

articles.title: Swedish finance minister prepares caretaker budget stripped of campaign promises
articles.summary: As Sweden doesn't yet have a new government, outgoing Finance Minister Elisabeth Svantesson will present a caretaker budget in November. It will be completely devoid of election pledges and fresh policy initiatives – except for one thing.

articles.title: Sweden's Centre Party leader: 'No majority for a centrist government'
articles.summary: Centre Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist is ending her bid to forge a centrist coalition and has handed her exploratory mandate back to the speaker of parliament.

articles.title: 'Generational rage': How young Europeans are fighting to be heard
articles.summary: From blockaded schools in Rome to tent camps in Madrid and street protests in France, young people across Europe are turning their anger on a political class they say is not listening.

articles.title: Why is it taking five years to develop language tests for Swedish citizenship?
articles.summary: Eighteen months after Stockholm University was instructed to develop language tests for citizenship, it has finally hired a project manager. Lars Bokander told The Local that when it comes to developing test items, he is "more or less starting from scratch".

articles.title: Sweden Democrat leader backs 'open Swedishness' amid high-profile party clash
articles.summary: Sweden Democrat leader Jimmie Åkesson has waded into an ongoing internal party row over what defines Swedish identity.

articles.title: What would it take for Swedish Migration Agency to freeze 'teen deportations'?
articles.summary: The Swedish Migration Agency will not freeze the controversial deportations of young adults – yet.

articles.title: 'He's the reason I'm here': Dad fights to stay in Sweden with baby son
articles.summary: A committed father was left 'speechless' by a Swedish Migration Court decision saying moving to 'visa-free visits' from the UK would not unduly affect his relationship with his one-year-old son. He is fighting the deportation order with a second appeal.

articles.title: Inside Sweden: Why force foreigners to leave Sweden to change their residency permit?
articles.summary: Richard Orange suggests that Sweden should stop splitting couples and families by forcing people to leave Sweden when applying for residency on new grounds, before running through the week's news.

articles.title: Sweden's centre-left bloc agrees on plan to halt teen deportations
articles.summary: Sweden's centre-left parties have reached an agreement on how to draft a emergency law halting so-called "teenage deportations".

articles.title: How did Swedish media cover the 'migration paradigm shift'?
articles.summary: Immigration was at the heart of the political debate in the past four years, but the voices of immigrants themselves were comparatively rarely centred in the media coverage, an analysis by The Fix Research & Advisory in partnership with The Local shows.

articles.title: 'I want to be with my husband': Pregnant woman forced to leave Sweden
articles.summary: Newly married and expecting her first child, it should be the happiest year of Brenda Ramström's life. But today she's going to have to get on a flight back home to Brazil, not knowing when she'll be able to reunite with her husband in Sweden.

articles.title: Foreign SSAB workers released as Dutch lawyer slams Swedish site raid
articles.summary: The 19 Filipino electrical engineers who were seized by Swedish police on October 9th and held in a Migration Agency detention centre have been released, with the company's lawyer calling the decision to detain them "unlawful" and promising to seek damages.

articles.title: All Swedish parties back emergency freeze on teen deportations
articles.summary: All parties in the Swedish parliament are backing a proposal to introduce emergency legislation halting the so-called 'teen deportations'. However, bringing the new law into force could take time.

articles.title: Swedish MP seeks to apply old rules to all pre-June 6th citizenship applicants
articles.summary: UPDATED: The Centre Party is willing to consider a new plan by Green Party MP Annika Hirvonen to allow everyone who applied for Swedish citizenship before June 6th – including those whose application has already been rejected – to be assessed under the old rules.

articles.title: How Sweden's 'new majority' can already move on deportations and citizenship
articles.summary: The Green Party's top MP Annika Hirvonen has started the new parliamentary term with a flurry of initiatives on teen deportations. She tells The Local how she hopes a new majority will allow action on citizenship and Brexit deportations too.

articles.title: Tech leader wins appeal under Sweden's new citizenship rules
articles.summary: The AI consultant Anna Bärlund is one of the first to successfully appeal a citizenship rejection under Sweden's new longer residency requirements. Her arguments won't work for everyone, but the ruling could have wider implications if upheld.

articles.title: OPINION: Sweden's Migration Agency is not fit for purpose. It should be scrapped
articles.summary: An interview by the The Local's Richard Orange with the Migration Agency's legal chief about Sweden’s large number of deportations of British people makes for depressing reading. It demonstrates why the agency is no longer capable of doing its job and now needs to be replaced, argues James Savage.

articles.title: Q&A: How will Sweden's new family immigration law affect researchers?
articles.summary: The previous Swedish government's law raising income requirements for foreigners with families in Sweden came into force on October 1st, 2026. The Local spoke to SULF, which represents higher education workers, about how researchers are affected.

articles.title: Lawyer warns Sweden's 'safety valve' could lead to new teen deportations
articles.summary: The bill Sweden's government has promoted as its solution to teen deportations has instead created a new group of young adults who risk being forced to leave Sweden, a lawyer has warned.

articles.title: Sweden's migration minister pledges long-term solution to teen deportations
articles.summary: The Swedish government wants to make permanent new temporary legislation aimed at stopping teenage deportations.

articles.title: Sweden's centre-left parties agree on halting teen deportations
articles.summary: Sweden's centre-left parties have reached an agreement on emergency legislation to halt teenage deportations.

articles.title: 'But what are the rules?': My interview with the Swedish Migration Agency's legal chief
articles.summary: When Richard Orange was granted an interview on Brexit rules with the Migration Agency's legal chief on his fourth attempt, it didn't exactly go as planned. But according to EU lawyers it nonetheless revealed flaws in the agency's grasp of EU law.

articles.title: Q&A: Who is affected by Sweden's new law on family immigration?
articles.summary: The previous Swedish government's law tightening rules for family reunification came into force on October 1st, 2026. The Local spoke to Ann-Kari Olsson, Section Head at the Swedish Migration Agency, to find out who is affected – and how.

articles.title: There are now more than 600,000 Gothenburgers living in Gothenburg
articles.summary: Sweden's second-largest city is now home to more than 600,000 people, new data shows.

articles.title: New rail service planned through Norway, Sweden and Denmark to Hamburg
articles.summary: Plans for a new rail service running from Oslo and stopping in Gothenburg, Malmö and Copenhagen before arriving in Hamburg are in the works, Swedish state-owned rail operator SJ has said.

articles.title: How jellyfish in Gothenburg's archipelago reveal impact of climate change
articles.summary: A global increase in jellyfish sparked by climate change is impacting communities in the Gothenburg archipelago, with local restaurants and fishing reporting the effects.

articles.title: Red-green coalition takes power in Gothenburg
articles.summary: The Social Democrats, Green Party and Left Party have managed to oust the right-wing Moderates from power in Gothenburg, despite failing to strike a coalition deal with the Centre Party.

articles.title: Gothenburg: is the dream of a new city turning into a nightmare?
articles.summary: Sweden’s second city is the site of Scandinavia’s largest urban development project. But there is rising concern that the costs outweigh the benefits, says David Crouch

articles.title: Why is Gothenburg known as Sweden’s 'Little London'?
articles.summary: With ties to Britain dating back more than 200 years, the city of Gothenburg has long been known as Sweden’s Little London.

articles.title: Volvo to invest 10 billion kronor in iconic Gothenburg factory
articles.summary: Volvo plans to invest 10 billion kronor in its Gothenburg plant in Sweden as it switches production to electric cars.

articles.title: Gothenburg apartment blast suspect found dead
articles.summary: Prosecutors have said that the man suspected as being behind a detonation in Gothenburg last week has been found dead on Wednesday after an apparent suicide.

articles.title: Gothenburg blast: Police identify suspect with 'no link to criminal gangs'
articles.summary: Police have confirmed that they have identified a suspect for the blast in Gothenburg earlier this week, which forced around 200 people to evacuate their homes and seriously injured four.

articles.title: Gothenburg blast: Here's what we do (and don't) know so far
articles.summary: UPDATED: Two people remained in intensive care on Wednesday after an apartment block explosion in Gothenburg the day before, which police said was likely not due to natural causes. Here's what we know about the incident.

articles.title: Gothenburg blast: Explosion 'not due to natural causes', say police
articles.summary: At least 16 people have been reportedly admitted to hospital after an explosion in an apartment building in central Gothenburg, which police are investigating as a potential crime.

articles.title: Floods and transport disruption after heavy rainfall across central Sweden
articles.summary: Heavy rainfall has led to hundreds of flooded buildings and roads in central Sweden that continue to disrupt traffic on Thursday.

articles.title: Moving to Gothenburg? The best areas and neighbourhoods to live in
articles.summary: Whether you're moving to Sweden’s second biggest city for the first time or are looking for another neighbourhood, The Local talks you through some of your best options.

articles.title: Spate of accidents as snow blankets western and southern Sweden
articles.summary: A snowstorm had on Thursday morning already caused several accidents in western Sweden, with authorities warning residents not to head out on the road.

articles.title: Western Sweden told to brace for heavy snow
articles.summary: Sweden's national weather agency SMHI has issued a warning for snowfall in southern Sweden, with western parts of the country expected to bear the brunt.

articles.title: Coronavirus: Western Swedish region steps up face mask recommendations to curb new outbreaks
articles.summary: New coronavirus recommendations urge people in Gothenburg and the rest of the Västra Götaland region to wear face masks on public transport at all times.

articles.title: Step back in time: 10 images that bring historic Gothenburg to life
articles.summary: Gothenburg in the first half of the 20th century was a very different – and surprisingly similar – city to what it is today. Let's take a look...

articles.title: Readers reveal: What you need to know about life in Gothenburg
articles.summary: We asked our readers what they like and dislike most about life on the west coast. Here's what you told us.

articles.title: Five great day trips to do from Gothenburg
articles.summary: Gothenburg has a lively culture scene, plenty of green spaces and food and drink in abundance, but sometimes you just need to escape the city. The West Coast and nearby towns provide plenty of opportunities for a memorable day trip from Sweden's second city: here are five of our favourite destinations complete with insider tips.

articles.title: The story of the biggest fire disaster in Swedish history
articles.summary: At a Halloween party in Gothenburg in 1998, a fire started by four youths led to one of the deadliest disasters of modern Swedish history. Sixty-three young people lost their lives and many more were injured.
